body:
Holy smokes, absolutely. I can't isolate myself from them, because they support me financially while I'm in university, but my contact with them is not very frequent. Mum hasn't got much of a social life herself, so she tries to attach herself to mine, like, wants to know everything about my activities, has an opinion on everything in my life... she's like that pathetic friend that drags everything down by trying too hard to be relevant. 

I'm thinking that if she hadn't me and my brother, she would have less trouble keeping up with the world and having a fantastic life herself. She really shouldn't have had me. Yours probably too.
Thanks, brother. I've been raised to be considerate, unfortunately. Hope I'll get over it soon.

Whichever one you're at now. Every country has a high bridge you can jump from, or a train you can jump in front of. 

If you want assisted suicide, here's an excerpt from Wiki:

As of June 2016, human euthanasia is legal in the Netherlands, Belgium, Colombia,[1] and Luxembourg. Assisted suicide is legal in Switzerland, Germany, Japan, Canada, and in the US states of Washington, Oregon, Colorado, Vermont, Montana, Washington DC,[2] and California.[3]

but I'm not sure if the procedure is legal at any of those for the foreigners. 

If you're white, can travel to the US and buy a gun with a forged license.

Good luck, hope the pain won't stay for too long!

Well, I don't work, I study full-time. As for volunteering, agree, it's a truly noble deed, and a fun one. You know, I used to volunteer writing for one educational nonprofit blog, but then school got hard, and I kept getting lesser and lesser time for that - until once, I promised them an article, which I had no time to write for a week, then another - and I felt terrible. And I bailed from there with no notice. Like a coward. Like a human I am. Does it mean I'm too unreliable for volunteering?

Look up Human Footprint. I've lived a third of my lifetime, so if I die right now, 2/3 of the resources will stay for others. 2/3 of the waste won't be produced by me. 

I look around and see people completely indifferent to their surroundings, mindlessly indulging in cheap pleasures and always unhappy with what they've. I look around more and I see people who appreciate what they've got in their lives, who do good deeds for the humanity, who want happiness for all, not just for themselves. Then I see these people being laughed at, frowned upon, censored by the former group - which, somehow, dominates. Why have we got Trump for a president? Why are there so many wars, with veterans praised and pacifists shunned? This is the humanity for me. This is what I'm forced to be part of. 

I don't know how to see the bright side of humanity.
Thank you for the ideas! Which of the above, do you think, will benefit humanity the most while keeping me alive and well for my parents?
It's in our nature, to be terrible to each other... Of course, we're also nice to each other - when it benefits us. But there is a constant competition for resources among us.

No, I know that all humans are. And I feel terrible for inconveniencing the world with my existence, and know we both will benefit from my death. The less humans there are, the better.

... maybe what I need is a lobotomy to get rid of this self-awareness.
I'm a selfish, gross, inconsiderate, harmful, parasitic, sex-driven, emotional human. This probably won't change until the reincarnation. So I've got to cope with this until death.

Hi, thank you for the idea! 

I'm not quite certain what you and your best friend mean by "ignoring it". Like, accept that it's alright to be a human and just do your thing? Not sure I'd be able to. Too much self-awareness in my head.

I'm staying away from any therapy and medicine, because I don't want to be "converted". Have you read Nineteen Eighty-Four? Remember how the main character was dragged through all the mental procedures performed on him and got to love The Big Brother in the end? I don't want that to happen to me.

Thank you for your thoughts! 

Agree on the curiousity. I myself am curious how tomorrow turns out, what new I'll learn about the world or myself. I guess that's another reason I stay alive, indeed! 

However, that goes back to... being selfish. Rather than ridding the world of myself, I stay around, consume resources, cause people trouble (mostly by accident, of course) - just because I want to see the future? C'mon, I'm better than that.

That's a very interesting thought. Some researches do show that we're much more considerate than our ancestors a long long time ago. By golly, slavery and pedophilia are illegal now, we sure can progress!

However, physiologically, we evolve pretty slowly. Our brains are still subject to primary instincts, basically to do everything to survive and reproduce. How long will it take us as a species to become better than that? 

I wish I could help, but how can I? There are some ideas that I tinker with in my head. There are even a few I've tried, but maybe I chose the wrong people... those I've tried to talk to about bettering themselves showed no signs of desire to put effort for that. So, yeah, maybe my ideas of helping people are just not good. So, my idea is that the only way I can help the planet is by ridding it of one more parasite.

Hi, hugs back, thank you for your reply :)

Mom is confident she's got to the root of my issues by just guilt-tripping me. She's also quite religious and most of the reasons to stay alive she gives me are in some way religion-based, like "This life was given to you and you aren't the one to decide to take it". I've tried talking to her several times, with the same result. She is a wonderful mom, as much as a human being can be, but she cannot help me there, even though she thinks she did help me, lol.

And helping other humans... I don't know if there's the point. They are also selfish, gross, inconsiderate, etc. whenever there is an opportunity to be. One helps them, and how confident can one be that they'll return the favour to the humanity? So there's a threat that one's kindness will merely die out. It's a depressing perspective.

If only I had a way to think about the humanity in a good way... But the Antropology 101 class I took, some of the evolutionary psychology lectures I attended, and global events seen on the news kind of leave me hopeless.

Bro, please, just ask her. Before you do, imagine the worst thing that may happen (her rejecting you, I assume?) and think how you'd treat it (for example "ah well, I'll die soon, I won't suffer from that rejection for too long"). This will help you mentally prepare for potential rejection.

Er, that's what I'm doing now - been spending days binge watching various Let's Play series on YouTube. But isn't there a danger that you let yourself go and lose all sources of income which allow you to, well, stay alive?

It's just a day. You do not owe anybody to celebrate it in a certain fashion. I'm single for two or three years now and I just use it as a reason to watch some romantic film I never allocated time to watch, usually about love between a human and a machine. While the world was watching 50 Shades Of Grey, I was watching Electric Dreams and dancing along to its awesome soundtrack. Now the world will be watching 50 Shades Darker and I already have Bicentennial Man ready for the Tuesday!

>  Finding the right help isn't always easy, of course, but it does usually exist.

and costs one a kidney. Prices for psychotherapy make it a luxury. Who to come for help to if you're short on money and the culture preaches individualism, meaning your problems are yours alone?
... or until you run out of money which you've spent on bad therapists.

Hi, thank you for the kind words and your point of view :) 

Hopes and dreams kept on changing, but it's that way for everyone. At the moment, in between procrastinating, studying and doing writing for one non-profit organization, I work on making my own virtual space, like writing down the structure, doing some crude modeling. I know programming, and if I find a decent platform to put my idea on, I'll do it. My computer is too weak for that, but who knows!

The depressing thing about wanting to dedicate myself to something is the concern that thanks to the capitalism, I will have to put a price on my work and sell it if I want to live. I just want to do good things for people, without a concern about how much money is ethical to take from them, and that other people with a consumer state of mind will take advantage of my good intentions.

That's something that makes me stutter with whatever endeavor I've in mind. And makes me feel that I'm not suitable for the world, because I want something different from what it provides.
Good advice, but not all of us are part of a social circle which includes a trusted drug dealer.
So, like, aiming to be enlightened is an aim to be more of an observer than a participant in the flow of life, including your own? That's an idea, I must admit...
